translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chenghua reign, his cap and belt were restored and he was allowed to live in retirement.

sentences.zh: 有貞既釋歸，猶冀帝復召，時時仰觀天象，謂將星在吳，益自負。

translations.literal: After Youzhen was released and returned home, he still hoped the emperor would summon him again; he often looked up to observe the celestial signs, saying the general's star was in Wu, and grew ever more self-confident.
translations.idiomatic: After Youzhen was released and returned home, he still hoped the emperor would summon him again; he often looked up to observe the celestial signs, saying the general's star was in Wu, and grew ever more self-confident.

sentences.zh: 常以鐵鞭自隨，數起舞。

translations.literal: He often carried an iron whip with him and frequently danced with it.
translations.idiomatic: He often carried an iron whip with him and frequently danced with it.

sentences.zh: 及聞韓雍征兩廣有功，乃擲鞭太息曰：「孺子亦應天象邪？」

translations.literal: When he heard that Han Yong had achieved merit in the campaign in the two Guang provinces, he threw down his whip and sighed: "Can a mere youth also answer to the celestial signs?
translations.idiomatic: When he heard that Han Yong had achieved merit in the campaign in the two Guang provinces, he threw down his whip and sighed: "Can a mere youth also answer to the celestial signs?

sentences.zh: 遂放浪山水間，十余年乃卒。

translations.literal: He then wandered freely among mountains and rivers, and more than ten years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: He then wandered freely among mountains and rivers, and more than ten years later he died.

sentences.zh: 有貞初出獄時，拊士權背曰：「子，義士也，他日一女相托。」

translations.literal: When Youzhen first left prison, he patted Shiquan on the back and said: "You are a man of honor; one day I shall entrust a daughter to you.
translations.idiomatic: When Youzhen first left prison, he patted Shiquan on the back and said: "You are a man of honor; one day I shall entrust a daughter to you.

sentences.zh: 金齒歸，士權時往候之，絕不及婚事。

translations.literal: When Youzhen returned from Jinchi, Shiquan often visited him but never mentioned the marriage.
translations.idiomatic: When Youzhen returned from Jinchi, Shiquan often visited him but never mentioned the marriage.

sentences.zh: 士權辭去，終身不言其事，人以是薄有貞而重士權。

translations.literal: When Shiquan took his leave, he never spoke of the matter for the rest of his life; people therefore looked down on Youzhen and respected Shiquan.
translations.idiomatic: When Shiquan took his leave, he never spoke of the matter for the rest of his life; people therefore looked down on Youzhen and respected Shiquan.

sentences.zh: 楊善，字思敬，大興人。

translations.literal: Yang Shan, styled Sijing, was a native of Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shan, courtesy name Sijing, came from Daxing.

sentences.zh: 年十七為諸生。

translations.literal: At the age of seventeen he became a student.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of seventeen he became a student.

sentences.zh: 成祖起兵，預城守有勞，授典儀所引禮舍人。

translations.literal: When the Yongle Emperor raised his army, Shan took part in the defense of the city with merit and was appointed Ceremonial Attendant of the Directorate of Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongle Emperor raised his army, Shan took part in the defense of the city with merit and was appointed Ceremonial Attendant of the Directorate of Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年，改鴻臚寺序班。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongle, he was transferred to Usher of the Court of State Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 1 (1403), he was transferred to Usher of the Court of State Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 善偉風儀，音吐洪亮，工進止。

translations.literal: Shan had a commanding presence, a resonant voice, and was skilled in deportment.
translations.idiomatic: Shan had a commanding presence, a resonant voice, and was skilled in deportment.

sentences.zh: 每朝謁引進奏時，上目屬之。

translations.literal: Whenever he led the court in paying homage and presenting memorials, the emperor's eyes would turn to him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he led the court in paying homage and presenting memorials, the emperor's eyes would turn to him.

sentences.zh: 累進右寺丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted step by step to Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted step by step to Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，擢本寺卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong ascended the throne, he was promoted to Director of the court.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong ascended the throne, he was promoted to Director of the court.

sentences.zh: 宣德六年被劾下獄，褫冠帶，逾月。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xuande he was impeached and thrown into prison; his cap and belt were stripped from him for more than a month.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 6 (1431), he was impeached and thrown into prison; his cap and belt were stripped from him for more than a month.

sentences.zh: 正統六年，子容詐作中官書，假金於尚書吳中。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhengtong, his son Rong forged a letter from a eunuch and borrowed gold from Minister Wu Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 6 (1441), his son Rong forged a letter from a eunuch and borrowed gold from Minister Wu Zhong.

sentences.zh: 事覺，謫戍威遠衛，置善不問。

translations.literal: When the affair was discovered, Rong was banished to garrison duty at Weiyuan Guard; Shan was not questioned.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was discovered, Rong was banished to garrison duty at Weiyuan Guard; Shan was not questioned.

sentences.zh: 久之，擢禮部左侍郎，仍視鴻臚事。

translations.literal: After some time he was promoted to Left Vice Minister of Rites while still overseeing the affairs of the Court of State Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: After a time he was promoted to Left Vice Minister of Rites while still overseeing the affairs of the Court of State Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 先是袁敏者，請賫服禦物問上皇安，不納。

translations.literal: Earlier, a man named Yuan Min had requested permission to carry imperial garments and goods to inquire after the former emperor's welfare; the request was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, a man named Yuan Min had requested permission to carry imperial garments and goods to inquire after the former emperor's welfare; the request was not accepted.

sentences.zh: 及是，尚書胡濙等言，上皇蒙塵久，禦用服食宜付善等隨行，亦不報。

translations.literal: At this time Minister Hu Ying and others stated that the former emperor had long been in captivity and that his imperial garments and food should be entrusted to Shan and others to carry with them; again there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Minister Hu Ying and others stated that the former emperor had long been in captivity and that his imperial garments and food should be entrusted to Shan and others to carry with them; again there was no response.

sentences.zh: 時也先欲還上皇，而敕書無奉迎語，自賫賜也先外，善等無他賜。

translations.literal: At that time Esen wished to return the former emperor, but the imperial letter contained no language of welcome; apart from gifts for Esen that they carried themselves, Shan and the others had no other presents.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Esen wished to return the former emperor, but the imperial letter contained no language of welcome; apart from gifts for Esen that they carried themselves, Shan and the others had no other presents.

sentences.zh: 善乃出家財，悉市彼中所需者，攜以往。

translations.literal: Shan thereupon spent his own family's wealth to buy everything needed in that region and carried it with him.
translations.idiomatic: Shan thereupon spent his own family's wealth to buy everything needed in that region and carried it with him.

sentences.zh: 既至，其館伴與飲帳中，詫善曰：「土木之役，六師何怯也？」

translations.literal: When they arrived, his Mongol host drank with him in the tent and said in astonishment to Shan: "At the Tumu campaign, why were the six armies so timid?
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived, his Mongol host drank with him in the tent and said in astonishment to Shan: "At the Tumu campaign, why were the six armies so timid?

sentences.zh: 善曰：「彼時官軍壯者悉南征，王司禮邀大駕幸其裏，不為戰備，故令汝得誌耳。

translations.literal: Shan said: "At that time all the strong troops of the government army were on the southern campaign; Director Wang invited the imperial carriage to visit his home district and made no war preparations, which is why you were able to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Shan said: "At that time all the strong troops of the government army were on the southern campaign; Director Wang invited the imperial carriage to visit his home district and made no war preparations, which is why you were able to succeed.

sentences.zh: 今南征將士歸，可二十萬。

translations.literal: Now the southern campaign troops have returned—some two hundred thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Now the southern campaign troops have returned—some two hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 又募中外材官技擊，可三十萬。

translations.literal: In addition, skilled fighters and martial artists from within and outside the court have been recruited—some three hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In addition, skilled fighters and martial artists from within and outside the court have been recruited—some three hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 悉教以神槍火器藥弩，百步外洞人馬腹立死。

translations.literal: All have been trained in divine guns, firearms, poisoned bolts, and crossbows that pierce men and horses through the belly at more than a hundred paces and kill them instantly.
translations.idiomatic: All have been trained in divine guns, firearms, poisoned bolts, and crossbows that pierce men and horses through the belly at more than a hundred paces and kill them instantly.

sentences.zh: 又用策士言，緣邊要害，隱鐵椎三尺，馬蹄踐輒穿。

translations.literal: Following the advice of strategists, three-foot iron spikes have been hidden at key points along the frontier; when horses' hooves tread on them, they pierce through.
translations.idiomatic: Following the advice of strategists, three-foot iron spikes have been hidden at key points along the frontier; when horses' hooves tread on them, they pierce through.

sentences.zh: 又刺客林立，夜度營幕若猿猱。」

translations.literal: Furthermore, assassins stand ready in great numbers, crossing camp tents at night like apes."
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, assassins stand ready in great numbers, crossing camp tents at night like apes."

sentences.zh: 伴色動。

translations.literal: The host's expression changed.
translations.idiomatic: The host's expression changed.

sentences.zh: 善曰：「惜哉，今皆置無用矣。」

translations.literal: Shan said: "What a pity—all of this is now set aside as useless.
translations.idiomatic: Shan said: "What a pity—all of this is now set aside as useless.

sentences.zh: 問：「何故？」

translations.literal: He asked: "Why?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked: "Why?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「和議成，歡好且若兄弟，安用此？」

translations.literal: Shan said: "Peace has been concluded, and our friendship is like that of brothers—what need is there for such things?"
translations.idiomatic: Shan said: "Peace has been concluded, and our friendship is like that of brothers—what need is there for such things?"

sentences.zh: 因以所賫遺之。

translations.literal: He then presented what he had brought as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He then presented what he had brought as gifts.

sentences.zh: 其人喜，悉以語也先。

translations.literal: The man was pleased and told Esen everything.
translations.idiomatic: The man was pleased and told Esen everything.

sentences.zh: 明日謁也先，亦大有所遺，也先亦喜。

translations.literal: The next day, when Shan paid his respects to Esen, he also gave many gifts, and Esen was pleased as well.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, when Shan paid his respects to Esen, he also gave many gifts, and Esen was pleased as well.

sentences.zh: 善因詰之曰：「太上皇帝朝，太師遣貢使必三千人，歲必再賚，金幣載途，乃背盟見攻何也？」

translations.literal: Shan then questioned him, saying: "During the reign of the Retired Emperor, the Grand Preceptor always sent tribute missions of three thousand men, and twice each year gifts were bestowed; gold and silks filled the roads—why then did you break the alliance and attack?
translations.idiomatic: Shan then questioned him: "During the reign of the Retired Emperor, the Grand Preceptor always sent tribute missions of three thousand men, and twice each year gifts were bestowed; gold and silks filled the roads—why then did you break the alliance and attack?

sentences.zh: 也先曰：「奈何削我馬價，予帛多剪裂，前後使人往多不歸，又減歲賜？」

translations.literal: Esen said: "Why was my horse price reduced, the silks given me mostly cut and torn, envoys sent back and forth mostly not returning, and the annual gifts reduced?"
translations.idiomatic: Esen said: "Why was my horse price reduced, the silks given me mostly cut and torn, envoys sent back and forth mostly not returning, and the annual gifts reduced?"

sentences.zh: 善曰：「非削也，太師馬歲增，價難繼而不忍拒，故微損之。

translations.literal: Shan said: "It was not a reduction; the Grand Preceptor's horses increase each year, and the price could not be sustained, yet we could not bear to refuse—therefore it was slightly reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Shan said: "It was not a reduction; the Grand Preceptor's horses increase each year, and the price could not be sustained, yet we could not bear to refuse—therefore it was slightly reduced.

sentences.zh: 太師自度，價比前孰多也？

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor, you yourself judge—which price is more than before?
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor, judge for yourself—is the price not higher than before?

sentences.zh: 帛剪裂者，通事為之，事露，誅矣。

translations.literal: As for the silks cut and torn, the interpreters did it; when the matter was exposed, they were executed.
translations.idiomatic: The cut and torn silks were the work of interpreters; when the affair came to light, they were put to death.

sentences.zh: 即太師貢馬有劣弱，貂或敝，亦豈太師意耶？

translations.literal: Even if among the Grand Preceptor's tribute horses there were weak ones, or sable furs that were worn, could that also have been the Grand Preceptor's intention?
translations.idiomatic: Even if some tribute horses were weak or some sable furs worn, could that truly have been the Grand Preceptor's wish?

sentences.zh: 且使者多至三四千人，有為盜或犯他法，歸恐得罪，故自亡耳，留若奚為？

translations.literal: Moreover, envoys often numbered as many as three or four thousand; some committed theft or violated other laws, and fearing punishment upon return, fled on their own—what purpose would keeping them serve?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the envoys often numbered three or four thousand; some stole or broke other laws and, fearing punishment when they returned home, simply fled—what would be gained by detaining them?

sentences.zh: 貢使受宴賜，上名或浮其人數，朝廷核實而予之。

translations.literal: When tribute envoys received feasts and gifts, the names submitted sometimes inflated the number of persons; the court verified and then granted accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: When tribute envoys received feasts and gifts, the rolls sometimes inflated their numbers; the court verified the head count before dispensing rewards.

sentences.zh: 所減乃虛數，有其人者，固不減也。」

translations.literal: What was reduced were only fictitious numbers; where persons actually existed, they were naturally not reduced."
translations.idiomatic: Only phantom figures were cut; anyone who actually existed was never shortchanged."

sentences.zh: 也先屢稱善。

translations.literal: Esen repeatedly expressed approval.
translations.idiomatic: Esen repeatedly expressed approval.

sentences.zh: 善復曰：「太師再攻我，屠戮數十萬，太師部曲死傷亦不少矣。

translations.literal: Shan again said: "The Grand Preceptor attacked us twice, slaughtering hundreds of thousands; the Grand Preceptor's followers also suffered no small casualties.
translations.idiomatic: Shan added: "The Grand Preceptor attacked us twice and slaughtered hundreds of thousands; your own followers also suffered heavy losses.

sentences.zh: 上天好生，太師好殺，故數有雷警。

translations.literal: Heaven loves life; the Grand Preceptor loves killing—therefore thunder has repeatedly warned.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven cherishes life, yet the Grand Preceptor delights in killing—that is why thunder has warned you again and again.

sentences.zh: 今還上皇，和好如故，中國金幣日至，兩國俱樂，不亦美乎？」

translations.literal: Now if the Retired Emperor is returned, friendship restored as before, China's gold and silks arriving daily, both states rejoicing—is that not splendid?
translations.idiomatic: Return the Retired Emperor now, restore friendship as before, and China's gold and silks will flow in daily—both realms will rejoice. Would that not be splendid?

sentences.zh: 也先曰：「敕書何以無奉迎語？」

translations.literal: Esen said: "Why does the imperial edict contain no language of welcoming reception?
translations.idiomatic: Esen said: "Why does the imperial edict contain no words of welcome?

sentences.zh: 善曰：「此欲成太師令名，使自為之。

translations.literal: Shan said: "This is meant to establish the Grand Preceptor's fine reputation, letting you do it yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Shan said: "This is meant to burnish the Grand Preceptor's reputation—so that you may do it yourself.

sentences.zh: 若載之敕書，是太師迫於朝命，非太師誠心也。」

translations.literal: If it were written in the edict, it would mean the Grand Preceptor acted under compulsion from court orders, not from the Grand Preceptor's own sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: If it were written into the edict, people would say the Grand Preceptor acted only under compulsion from the court, not from his own heart.

sentences.zh: 也先大喜，問：「上皇歸將復得為天子乎？」

translations.literal: Esen was greatly pleased and asked: "When the Retired Emperor returns, will he again become Son of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Esen was greatly pleased and asked: "When the Retired Emperor returns, will he again become emperor?

sentences.zh: 善曰：「天位已定，難再移。」

translations.literal: Shan said: "The heavenly throne is already fixed; it is hard to move again.
translations.idiomatic: Shan said: "The Mandate's seat is already settled; it cannot easily be moved again.

sentences.zh: 也先曰：「堯、舜如何？」

translations.literal: Esen said: "What of Yao and Shun?
translations.idiomatic: Esen said: "What of Yao and Shun?

sentences.zh: 善曰：「堯讓舜，今兄讓弟，正相同也。」

translations.literal: Shan said: "Yao yielded to Shun; now an elder brother yields to a younger brother—it is exactly the same.
translations.idiomatic: Shan said: "Yao yielded the throne to Shun; now an elder brother yields to a younger brother—the principle is the same.

sentences.zh: 其平章昂克問善：「何不以重寶來購？」

translations.literal: His pingzhang Angke asked Shan: "Why not bring heavy treasures to ransom him?
translations.idiomatic: His counselor Angke asked Shan: "Why not bring heavy treasure to buy him back?

sentences.zh: 善曰：「若賫貨來，人謂太師圖利。

translations.literal: Shan said: "If one brought goods as tribute to purchase him, people would say the Grand Preceptor schemed for profit.
translations.idiomatic: Shan said: "If we brought treasure to ransom him, people would say the Grand Preceptor acted for gain.

sentences.zh: 今不爾，乃見太師仁義，為好男子，垂史策，頌揚萬世。」

translations.literal: Now acting otherwise, one shows the Grand Preceptor's benevolence and righteousness, proves oneself a man of honor, wins a place in the historical records, and is praised for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Act otherwise, and you show the Grand Preceptor's benevolence and righteousness—a true man of honor, whose name will live in the histories and be praised for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 也先笑稱善。

translations.literal: Esen laughed and expressed approval.
translations.idiomatic: Esen laughed and expressed approval.

sentences.zh: 知院伯毅帖木耳勸也先留使臣，而遣使要上皇復位。

translations.literal: Commissioner Bo Yitiemuer urged Esen to detain the envoys and send a messenger demanding the Retired Emperor's restoration to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner Bo Yitiemuer urged Esen to hold the envoys and send a messenger demanding the Retired Emperor's restoration.

sentences.zh: 也先懼失信，不可，竟許善奉上皇還。

translations.literal: Esen feared breaking faith and would not agree; in the end he permitted Shan to escort the Retired Emperor home.
translations.idiomatic: Esen feared to break his word and refused; in the end he allowed Shan to escort the Retired Emperor home.

sentences.zh: 時舉朝競奇善功，而景帝以非初遣旨，薄其賞。

translations.literal: At the time the whole court competed to marvel at Shan's achievement, but the Jing Emperor, because it was not the original dispatch's intent, slighted his reward.
translations.idiomatic: The whole court marveled at Shan's achievement, but the Jing Emperor held his reward to a minimum, on the ground that it had not been the purpose of the original mission.

sentences.zh: 遷左都御史，仍蒞鴻臚事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Censor-in-Chief, still overseeing Honglu affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief while continuing to oversee the Court of State Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 二年，廷臣朝正旦畢，修賀朝房。

translations.literal: In the second year, after court ministers finished the New Year's Day audience, they repaired the congratulatory assembly halls.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, after the court had finished the New Year's Day audience, the ministers refurbished the congratulatory reception halls.

sentences.zh: 善又曰：「上皇不受賀，我曹何相賀也？」

translations.literal: Shan again said: "The Retired Emperor does not receive congratulations—why should we congratulate one another?
translations.idiomatic: Shan said again: "The Retired Emperor does not accept congratulations—why should we congratulate one another?

sentences.zh: 三年正月加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the third year, first month, he was appointed Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 六年以衰老乞致仕，優詔不許。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, citing age and infirmity he requested retirement; a favorably worded edict refused permission.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he petitioned to retire on account of age and infirmity; an edict graciously refused.

sentences.zh: 善負才辨，以巧取功名，而憸忮為士論所棄。

translations.literal: Shan relied on talent and eloquence, winning fame and office by cunning, yet his malice and jealousy caused him to be rejected by scholarly opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Shan traded on talent and eloquence to win rank and renown by artifice, but his spite and jealousy left him scorned among the literati.

sentences.zh: 其為序班，坐事與庶吉士章樸同系獄，久之，相狎。

translations.literal: When he was an usher by rank, he was imprisoned for an offense together with the editorial graduate Zhang Pu; after a long time they grew familiar.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as an usher, he was imprisoned for an offense together with the Hanlin probationer Zhang Pu; after a long confinement they grew close.

sentences.zh: 時方窮治方孝孺黨，樸言家有孝孺集，未及毀。

translations.literal: At the time the court was rigorously prosecuting Fang Xiaoru's faction; Pu said his family possessed Fang's collected works, not yet destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then hunting down Fang Xiaoru's partisans; Pu mentioned that his family still possessed Fang's collected writings, not yet destroyed.

sentences.zh: 善從借觀，密奏之。

translations.literal: Shan borrowed them to read and secretly reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Shan borrowed the collection to read it and secretly reported the matter.

sentences.zh: 樸以是誅死，而善得復官。

translations.literal: Pu was executed for this, while Shan regained his office.
translations.idiomatic: Pu was executed for this, and Shan was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 于謙、王文之戮，陳循之竄，善亦有力焉。

translations.literal: In the executions of Yu Qian and Wang Wen and the exile of Chen Xun, Shan also had a hand.
translations.idiomatic: Shan also had a hand in the executions of Yu Qian and Wang Wen and the exile of Chen Xun.

sentences.zh: 子宗襲爵，後革「奪門」功，降金吾指揮使。

translations.literal: His son Zong inherited the title; later the "Storming the Gate" merit was revoked, and he was reduced to Commander of the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zong inherited the title; later, when the "Storming the Gate" honors were revoked, he was reduced to commander of the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 孫增尚公主。

translations.literal: His grandson Zeng married a princess.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Zeng married an imperial princess.

sentences.zh: 李實，字孟誠，合州人。

translations.literal: Li Shi, courtesy name Mengcheng, was a native of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi, styled Mengcheng, was a native of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 正統七年進士。

translations.literal: Metropolitan graduate in Zhengtong 7.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the seventh year of Zhengtong.

sentences.zh: 為人恣肆無拘檢，有口辨。

translations.literal: By nature he was unrestrained and without self-discipline, and had a glib tongue.
translations.idiomatic: He was by nature unrestrained and undisciplined, with a ready tongue for debate.

sentences.zh: 景泰初，為禮科給事中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingtai reign, he served as supervising secretary in the Bureau of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Jingtai reign he served as a supervising secretary in the Bureau of Rites.

sentences.zh: 也先令完者脫歡議和，實請行。

translations.literal: Esen had Oqir Taqi negotiate peace; Shi requested to go.
translations.idiomatic: When Esen had Oirat Taqi open peace talks, Shi volunteered to go.

sentences.zh: 擢禮部右侍郎以往，少卿羅綺為副。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites and sent, with Vice Director Luo Qi as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites and dispatched, with Vice Director Luo Qi as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 至則見上皇，頗得也先要領，還言也先請和無他意。

translations.literal: Upon arrival he met the Retired Emperor, grasped Esen's essential demands fairly well, and on returning said Esen's peace overtures had no other intent.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he met the Retired Emperor, gained a fair grasp of Esen's demands, and reported on his return that Esen's peace overtures had no ulterior motive.

sentences.zh: 及楊善往，上皇果還。

translations.literal: When Yang Shan went, the Retired Emperor indeed returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Shan went, the Retired Emperor was indeed brought home.

sentences.zh: 是年十月進右都御史，巡撫湖廣。

translations.literal: That year in the tenth month he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief and made grand coordinator of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of that year he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief and appointed grand coordinator of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 五年召還，掌院事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was recalled and took charge of censorate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was recalled to head the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 初，實使謁上皇，請還京引咎自責，失上皇意。

translations.literal: Initially, when Shi as envoy visited the Retired Emperor, he asked to return to the capital to confess fault and blame himself, losing the Retired Emperor's favor.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, on his mission Shi had visited the Retired Emperor and asked to return to the capital to confess guilt and accept blame, which lost him the Retired Emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 後以居鄉暴橫，斥為民。

translations.literal: Later, for violent misconduct while living at home, he was reduced to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for violent misconduct while at home, he was stripped of rank and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 趙榮，字孟仁，其先西域人。

translations.literal: Zhao Rong, courtesy name Mengren—his ancestors were Western Region people.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Rong, styled Mengren, came of Western Region stock.

sentences.zh: 元時入中國，家閩縣。

translations.literal: During the Yuan they entered China and made their home in Min County.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuan they entered China and settled in Min County.

sentences.zh: 舅薩琦，官翰林，從入都，以能書授中書舍人。

translations.literal: His maternal uncle Sa Qi served at Hanlin; following him into the capital, Rong was appointed a draft clerk in the Secretariat for his skill in calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: His maternal uncle Sa Qi held office at Hanlin; Rong followed him to the capital and, for his skill in calligraphy, was appointed a drafting clerk in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 正統十四年十月，也先擁上皇至大同，知府霍瑄謁見，慟哭而返。

translations.literal: In Zhengtong 14, tenth month, Esen brought the Retired Emperor to Datong; Prefect Huo Xuan went to pay respects, wept bitterly, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fourteenth year of Zhengtong, Esen brought the Retired Emperor to Datong; Prefect Huo Xuan went to pay his respects, wept bitterly, and returned.

sentences.zh: 也先遂犯京師，奉上皇登土城，邀大臣出迓。

translations.literal: Esen then invaded the capital, escorted the Retired Emperor onto the earthen rampart, and invited ministers to come out to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Esen then pressed on to the capital, brought the Retired Emperor up onto the earthen rampart, and summoned the ministers to come out and receive him.

sentences.zh: 榮慨然請行。

translations.literal: Rong passionately volunteered to go.
translations.idiomatic: Rong stepped forward and volunteered.

sentences.zh: 大學士高谷拊其背曰：「子，忠義人也。」

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Gao Gu patted his back and said: "You are a man of loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Gao Gu clapped him on the back and said: "You are a man of loyalty and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 解所佩犀帶贈之，即擢大理右少卿，充鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: He unfastened the rhinoceros-horn belt at his waist and gave it to him, immediately promoting him to Vice Director of the Dali Court and appointing him Protocol Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He unfastened the rhinoceros-horn belt at his waist and gave it to him, then immediately promoted him to Vice Director of the Dali Court and appointed him Protocol Secretary.

sentences.zh: 偕右通政王復出城朝見，進羊酒諸物。

translations.literal: Together with Vice Commissioner Wang Fu he went out of the city to pay audience, presenting sheep, wine, and other goods.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Vice Commissioner Wang Fu he went outside the city to pay audience, presenting sheep, wine, and other gifts.

sentences.zh: 也先以非大臣，遣之還，而邀于謙、石亨、王直、胡濙出。

translations.literal: Esen sent them back because they were not grand ministers, and instead invited Yu Qian, Shi Heng, Wang Zhi, and Hu Ying to come out.
translations.idiomatic: Esen sent them back on the ground that they were not senior ministers, and instead demanded that Yu Qian, Shi Heng, Wang Zhi, and Hu Ying come out.

sentences.zh: 景帝不遣。

translations.literal: The Jing Emperor did not send them.
translations.idiomatic: The Jing Emperor refused to send them.

sentences.zh: 改榮太常少卿，仍供事內閣。

translations.literal: Rong was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, still serving in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices while continuing to serve in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年七月擢工部右侍郎，偕楊善等往。

translations.literal: In Jingtai 1, seventh month, he was promoted to Vice Minister of Works and went together with Yang Shan and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the first year of Jingtai he was promoted to Vice Minister of Works and went with Yang Shan and others.

sentences.zh: 敕書無奉迎語，善口辯，榮左右之，竟奉上皇歸。

translations.literal: The edict contained no welcoming language; Shan was eloquent, Rong assisted on both sides, and in the end they escorted the Retired Emperor home.
translations.idiomatic: The edict bore no words of welcome; Shan was eloquent and Rong supported him, and in the end they escorted the Retired Emperor home.

sentences.zh: 進左侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 行人王晏請開沁河通漕運，再下廷議，言不便，遣榮往勘。

translations.literal: Clerk Wang Yan requested opening the Qin River to connect grain transport; after repeated court discussion saying it was impractical, Rong was sent to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Clerk Wang Yan proposed opening the Qin River to link the grain transport route; after repeated court debate found the plan impractical, Rong was sent to inspect the site.

sentences.zh: 還，亦言不便。

translations.literal: On returning, he also reported it impractical.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he too reported that it would not work.

sentences.zh: 尋奉敕會山東、河南三司相度河道。

translations.literal: Soon he received orders to meet with the three provincial offices of Shandong and Henan to survey the river course.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he received orders to join the three provincial offices of Shandong and Henan in surveying the river course.

sentences.zh: 眾以榮不由科目，慢之。

translations.literal: The assembly looked down on Rong because he had not come up through the examination route.
translations.idiomatic: The officials looked down on Rong because he had not risen through the examination system.

sentences.zh: 榮怒，多所撻辱，又自攝衣探水深淺。

translations.literal: Rong grew angry, beat and humiliated many, and personally rolled up his robes to probe the water's depth.
translations.idiomatic: Rong flew into a rage, beat and humiliated many of them, and even rolled up his own robes to test the depth of the water.

sentences.zh: 三司各上章言榮單馬馳走，驚駭軍民，杖傷縣官，鬻廩米多取其直。

translations.literal: The three offices each memorialized that Rong galloped alone, alarming soldiers and civilians, beat county officials with rods, and sold granary rice taking excessive payment.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the three provincial offices memorialized that Rong had ridden alone at full gallop, terrifying soldiers and civilians, beaten county officials with rods, and sold granary rice at inflated prices.

sentences.zh: 撫、按薛希璉、張琛亦以聞。

translations.literal: The grand coordinators and surveillance commissioners Xue Xilian and Zhang Chen also reported it.
translations.idiomatic: The grand coordinator and surveillance commissioner, Xue Xilian and Zhang Chen, reported the matter as well.

sentences.zh: 章下治河僉都御史徐有貞核奏。

translations.literal: The memorials were sent down to Xu Youzhen, the Censor and Commissioner for River Works, for verification and report.
translations.idiomatic: The memorials were referred to Xu Youzhen, the Censor-in-Chief in charge of river works, for investigation and report.

sentences.zh: 法司言，榮雖失大體，終為急於國事，鬻米從人所為。

translations.literal: The judicial offices said that although Rong had lost proper decorum, in the end he had been urgent about state affairs, and selling grain was done by his followers.
translations.idiomatic: The judicial offices held that although Rong had overstepped propriety, he had been zealous for state business, and the sale of grain had been done by his attendants.

sentences.zh: 諸臣侮大臣，抗敕旨，宜逮治，希璉、琛亦宜罪。

translations.literal: The various officials had insulted a grand minister and resisted imperial orders—they should be arrested and punished; Xilian and Chen should also be punished.
translations.idiomatic: The officials had insulted a senior minister and defied an imperial order—they should be arrested and punished; Xilian and Chen deserved punishment as well.

sentences.zh: 帝令按臣責取諸臣供狀，宥之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the investigating commissioners to require written confessions from the officials and pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the investigating commissioners to take written confessions from the officials and pardoned them.

sentences.zh: 霍瑄，字廷璧，鳳翔人。

translations.literal: Huo Xuan, courtesy name Tingbi, was a native of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Xuan, styled Tingbi, was a native of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 由鄉舉入國學，授大同通判。

translations.literal: Through county recommendation he entered the Imperial Academy and was appointed Vice Prefect of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended through the county examination, he entered the Imperial Academy and was appointed vice prefect of Datong.

sentences.zh: 正統十二年，以武進伯朱冕薦，就擢知府。

translations.literal: In Zhengtong 12, on recommendation of Marquis Wu Jin Zhu Mian, he was directly promoted to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Zhengtong, on the recommendation of Marquis Wu Jin Zhu Mian, he was promoted directly to prefect.

sentences.zh: 也先擁英宗至城下，瑄與理餉侍郎沈固等出謁，叩馬號泣。

translations.literal: When Esen brought Emperor Yingzong to the city wall, Xuan went out with Grain Supply Vice Minister Shen Gu and others to pay respects, beating upon the horse and wailing.
translations.idiomatic: When Esen brought Emperor Yingzong to the foot of the city wall, Xuan went out with Vice Minister of Grain Supply Shen Gu and others to pay respects, clinging to the horse and wailing.

sentences.zh: 眾露刃叱之，不為動。

translations.literal: The crowd bared blades and shouted at him, but he did not stir.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy bared their blades and shouted at him, but he did not flinch.

sentences.zh: 上皇命括城內金帛，瑄悉所有獻之，上皇嘉嘆。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor ordered the collection of gold and silks within the city; Xuan presented everything he possessed, and the Retired Emperor praised him with sighs.
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor ordered gold and silks gathered within the city; Xuan presented everything he owned, and the Retired Emperor praised him warmly.

sentences.zh: 寇數出沒大同、渾源，伺軍民樵采，輒驅掠。

translations.literal: Bandits repeatedly appeared and vanished around Datong and Hunyuan, watching for soldiers and civilians gathering firewood, then driving them off and plundering.
translations.idiomatic: Raiders repeatedly struck around Datong and Hunyuan, lying in wait for soldiers and civilians out gathering firewood, then driving them off and looting them.

sentences.zh: 或幸脫歸，率殘傷肢體。

translations.literal: Those who luckily escaped returned mostly maimed in their limbs.
translations.idiomatic: Those who escaped returned maimed more often than not.

sentences.zh: 遺民相率入城，無所棲，又乏食。

translations.literal: Surviving people entered the city in groups, with nowhere to dwell and lacking food.
translations.idiomatic: Survivors streamed into the city in groups, with nowhere to live and no food to eat.

sentences.zh: 瑄俱為奏之。

translations.literal: Xuan memorialized on all of these matters.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan memorialized on all these matters.

sentences.zh: 老弱聽暫徙，發粟振，而所留城守丁壯除賦役。

translations.literal: The aged and weak were permitted temporary relocation; grain was issued for relief, and able-bodied men who remained to defend the city were exempted from taxes and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: The aged and weak were allowed to relocate temporarily, grain was issued for relief, and able-bodied men who remained to defend the city were exempted from taxes and corvée labor.

sentences.zh: 秩滿當遷，鎮巡諸臣乞留。

translations.literal: When his term expired and he was due for transfer, the garrison and touring officials requested he remain.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired and he was due for transfer, the garrison and touring officials petitioned to keep him.

sentences.zh: 詔加山西右參政，仍治府事。

translations.literal: An edict added him Right Assistant Commissioner in Shanxi while he still governed the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made him Right Assistant Commissioner of Shanxi while he continued to govern the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 英宗復位，征拜瑄工部右侍郎，而固亦以石亨薦，起為戶部尚書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong was restored, Xuan was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of Works; Gu also, on Shi Heng's recommendation, was raised to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong was restored to the throne, Xuan was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of Works; Shen Gu, on Shi Heng's recommendation, was recalled as Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 既而巡撫上瑄治行，賜誥旌異。

translations.literal: Soon after, the grand coordinator reported Xuan's administrative record, and he was granted an edict of commendation for distinction.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the grand coordinator submitted a report on Xuan's governance, and he was granted an edict of commendation for outstanding service.

sentences.zh: 初，瑄在大同，巡撫年富被逮，瑄資其家還裏，為鎮守太監韋力轉所惡，撻之十余。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xuan was in Datong, Grand Coordinator Nian Fu was arrested; Xuan funded his family's return home, for which Garrison Eunuch Wei Lizhuan hated him and beat him more than ten times.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Xuan was in Datong, Grand Coordinator Nian Fu was arrested; Xuan paid for his family's journey home, for which Garrison Eunuch Wei Lizhuan took offense and had him beaten more than ten times.

sentences.zh: 至是瑄以聞，且言力轉每宴輒用妓樂，服禦僭侈如王者，強取部民女為妾。

translations.literal: At this time Xuan reported it, also saying Lizhuan always used singing girls and musicians at banquets, dressed and lived with regal extravagance, and forcibly took local girls as concubines.
translations.idiomatic: At this point Xuan reported the matter, adding that Lizhuan always entertained with singing girls and musicians at his banquets, dressed and lived with regal extravagance, and forcibly took local girls as concubines.

sentences.zh: 力轉亦訐瑄違法事。

translations.literal: Lizhuan also denounced Xuan for illegal acts.
translations.idiomatic: Lizhuan in turn denounced Xuan for unlawful conduct.

sentences.zh: 帝兩釋焉。

translations.literal: The emperor released both from punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pardoned them both.

sentences.zh: 其年轉左，賜二品服。

translations.literal: That year he was transferred to the left ministry and granted second-rank robes.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was transferred to the left vice ministry and granted second-rank robes.

sentences.zh: 成化初，屢為言官所劾。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chenghua reign, he was repeatedly impeached by censorial officials.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Chenghua reign he was repeatedly impeached by censorial officials.

sentences.zh: 命致仕。

translations.literal: He was ordered to retire.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to retire from office.

sentences.zh: 卒於京師。

translations.literal: He died in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the capital.

sentences.zh: 瑄初治郡有聲，晚節不檢。

translations.literal: Xuan at first governed his prefecture with renown; in his later years he was unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan had won renown in his early governance of the prefecture, but his later years were unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 特以艱危時見知天子，遂久列顯位。

translations.literal: Only because he won the emperor's notice in a time of peril did he long hold eminent office.
translations.idiomatic: He held high office for so long only because he had won the emperor's favor in a time of crisis.

sentences.zh: 沈固，丹陽人。

translations.literal: Shen Gu was a man of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Gu was a native of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 永樂中，起家鄉舉，積官至尚書。

translations.literal: In the Yongle reign he rose through provincial recommendation and, by accumulated promotion, reached the office of Minister.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongle reign he entered official life through provincial recommendation and rose step by step to become a minister.

sentences.zh: 石亨敗，乞休去。

translations.literal: When Shi Heng fell, he requested leave to retire.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Heng was overthrown, he asked to retire from office.

sentences.zh: 王越，字世昌，濬人。

translations.literal: Wang Yue, styled Shichang, was a man of Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue, courtesy name Shichang, was a native of Jun.

sentences.zh: 長身，多力善射。

translations.literal: He was tall of stature, strong, and skilled at archery.
translations.idiomatic: He was tall and powerfully built, and an excellent archer.

sentences.zh: 涉書史，有大略。

translations.literal: He had read books and histories and possessed great strategic vision.
translations.idiomatic: Well versed in history and the classics, he had a broad strategic mind.

sentences.zh: 登景泰二年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of the Jingtai reign.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in 1451, the second year of the Jingtai reign.

sentences.zh: 廷試日，旋風起，揚其卷去，更給卷，乃畢事。

translations.literal: On the day of the palace examination a whirlwind arose and blew his paper away; another paper was given him, and only then did he finish.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the palace examination a whirlwind suddenly sprang up and swept his examination paper away; he was given a fresh paper and at last completed the test.

sentences.zh: 授御史，出按陜西。

translations.literal: He was appointed censor and sent out to inspect Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a censor and dispatched on an inspection tour of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 聞父訃，不俟代輒歸，為都御史所劾。

translations.literal: On hearing of his father's death, he returned without waiting for a replacement and was impeached by the censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When word came of his father's death, he went home without waiting for a successor and was impeached by the censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 帝特原之。

translations.literal: The emperor specially pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally granted him pardon.

sentences.zh: 天順初，起掌諸道章奏，超拜山東按察使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianshun reign he was recalled to take charge of memorials from all circuits and was promoted directly to Shandong surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tianshun reign he was recalled to handle memorials from all provincial circuits and was promoted directly to surveillance commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 七年，大同巡撫都御史韓雍召還，帝難其代，喟然曰：「安得如雍者而任之。」

translations.literal: In the seventh year Han Yong, grand coordinator and censor-in-chief of Datong, was recalled; the emperor found it hard to replace him and sighed, saying, "Where can I find another like Yong to appoint?
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Han Yong, the grand coordinator and censor-in-chief at Datong, was recalled to court. The emperor struggled to find a successor and sighed, "Where can I find someone like Yong to put in that post?

sentences.zh: 李賢薦越，召見。

translations.literal: Li Xian recommended Yue, and he was summoned for an audience.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian recommended Wang Yue, and the emperor summoned him for an audience.

sentences.zh: 越偉服短袂，進止便利。

translations.literal: Yue was imposing in short-sleeved dress, and his movements were agile.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue cut an imposing figure in short military sleeves, and his bearing was quick and assured.

sentences.zh: 帝喜，擢右副都御史以行。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and promoted him to right vice censor-in-chief and sent him out.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, the emperor promoted him to right vice censor-in-chief and dispatched him to the post.

sentences.zh: 甫至，遭母憂，奪情視事。

translations.literal: Hardly had he arrived when he met with his mother's death; he was compelled to remain in mourning while continuing in office.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely taken up the post when his mother died; he was ordered to remain on duty despite the mourning period.

sentences.zh: 越乃繕器甲，簡卒伍，修堡寨，減課勸商，為經久計。

translations.literal: Yue then repaired weapons and armor, selected troops, restored forts and stockades, reduced levies and encouraged trade, and made long-term plans.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue set about repairing arms and armor, drilling the ranks, rebuilding forts and stockades, cutting taxes to encourage commerce, and laying plans for lasting defense.

sentences.zh: 成化三年，撫寧侯朱永征毛裏孩，以越贊理軍務。

translations.literal: In the third year of the Chenghua reign the Marquis of Funing, Zhu Yong, campaigned against Molihai, with Yue assisting in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1467, the third year of the Chenghua reign, the Marquis of Funing, Zhu Yong, marched against Molihai, with Wang Yue assisting in the management of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 其秋，兼巡撫宣府。

translations.literal: That autumn he also served concurrently as grand coordinator of Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was given the additional post of grand coordinator of Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 五年冬，寇入河套，延綏巡撫王銳請濟師，詔越帥師赴之。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifth year the raiders entered the Ordos Loop; Wang Rui, grand coordinator of Yan-sui, requested reinforcements, and an edict ordered Yue to lead troops to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fifth year raiders entered the Ordos region; Wang Rui, grand coordinator of Yan-sui, asked for reinforcements, and the court ordered Wang Yue to lead an army to his support.

sentences.zh: 河套者，周朔方、秦河南地，土沃，豐水草。

translations.literal: The Ordos Loop was the land of Shuofang under Zhou and Henan under Qin; its soil was rich and its grass and water abundant.
translations.idiomatic: The Ordos region was the ancient land of Shuofang under the Zhou and of Henan under the Qin—fertile soil with rich pasture and ample water.

sentences.zh: 東距山西偏頭關，西距寧夏，可二千里。

translations.literal: East it reached Piantou Pass in Shanxi; west it reached Ningxia; it was about two thousand li across.
translations.idiomatic: It stretched from Piantou Pass in Shanxi on the east to Ningxia on the west—a span of roughly two thousand li.

sentences.zh: 三面阻河，北拊榆林之背。

translations.literal: On three sides it was blocked by the river, and on the north it pressed against the rear of Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River hemmed it in on three sides, while to the north it lay hard against the rear of Yulin.

sentences.zh: 唐三受降城在河外，故內地。

translations.literal: Under Tang the three cities for receiving surrender lay beyond the river, so it was inner territory.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang the three surrender cities lay beyond the river, so the region had counted as inner territory.

sentences.zh: 明初，阻河為守，延綏亦無事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Ming, holding the river as defense, Yan-sui was also untroubled.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Ming the frontier was held along the river, and Yan-sui too remained quiet.

sentences.zh: 自天順間，毛裏孩等三部始入為寇，然時出沒，不敢久駐。

translations.literal: From the Tianshun period Molihai and the other three divisions first entered as raiders, yet they came and went and did not dare remain long.
translations.idiomatic: From the Tianshun period onward Molihai and three allied divisions began raiding across the border, but they appeared only intermittently and did not dare stay for long.

sentences.zh: 至是始屯牧其中，屢為邊患。

translations.literal: Only now did they begin to settle and graze there, repeatedly becoming a border affliction.
translations.idiomatic: By this time they had begun to settle and graze there in earnest, and the frontier suffered repeated raids.

sentences.zh: 越至榆林，遣遊擊將軍許寧出西路龍州、鎮靖諸堡，範瑾出東路神木、鎮羌諸堡，而自與中官秦剛按榆林城為聲援。

translations.literal: When Yue reached Yulin, he sent the mobile commander Xu Ning out by the western route through the forts of Longzhou and Zhenjing, Fan Jin out by the eastern route through the forts of Shenmu and Zhenqiang, and himself with the eunuch Qin Gang held Yulin city as a supporting force.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Yue reached Yulin, he sent the mobile commander Xu Ning by the western route through the forts at Longzhou and Zhenjing, Fan Jin by the eastern route through Shenmu and Zhenqiang, and himself remained at Yulin with the eunuch Qin Gang to hold the city as a reserve.

sentences.zh: 寧戰黎家澗，瑾戰崖窯川，皆捷；

translations.literal: Ning fought at Lijiajian and Jin at Yayaokou; both were victorious;
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ning fought at Lijiajian and Fan Jin at Yayaokou; both won victories;

sentences.zh: 右參將神英又破敵於鎮羌，寇乃退。

translations.literal: the right assistant commander Shen Ying again defeated the enemy at Zhenqiang, and the raiders then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: and the right assistant commander Shen Ying routed the enemy again at Zhenqiang, after which the raiders withdrew.

sentences.zh: 明年正月以捷聞，越引還。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year the victory was reported; Yue led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year news of the victory was sent to court, and Wang Yue led his troops back.

sentences.zh: 抵偏頭關，延綏告警。

translations.literal: When he reached Piantou Pass, Yan-sui raised the alarm.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Piantou Pass, an alarm came from Yan-sui.

sentences.zh: 兵部劾越擅還。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War impeached Yue for returning on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War impeached Wang Yue for withdrawing without authorization.

sentences.zh: 詔弗罪，而令越屯延綏近地為援。

translations.literal: An edict did not punish him but ordered Yue to encamp near Yan-sui as reinforcement.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declined to punish him and instead ordered Wang Yue to encamp near Yan-sui as a reserve force.

sentences.zh: 寇萬余騎五路入掠，越令寧等擊退之。

translations.literal: More than ten thousand mounted raiders entered by five routes to plunder; Yue ordered Ning and the others to strike and drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand mounted raiders entered in five columns to plunder; Wang Yue ordered Xu Ning and the others to beat them back.

sentences.zh: 進右副都御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 是年三月，朝廷以阿羅出等擾邊不止，拜撫寧侯朱永為將軍，與越共圖之。

translations.literal: In the third month of that year, because Alacu and others would not cease harassing the border, the court appointed the Marquis of Funing, Zhu Yong, as general to join Yue in planning against them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of that year, with Alacu and his allies still raiding the frontier without letup, the court appointed the Marquis of Funing, Zhu Yong, as commanding general to join Wang Yue in dealing with them.

sentences.zh: 破敵開荒川，諸將追奔至牛家寨，阿羅出中流矢走。

translations.literal: They defeated the enemy at Kaihuangchuan; the generals pursued the fleeing foe to Niujiazhai, and Alacu was struck by an arrow in flight and fled.
translations.idiomatic: They routed the enemy at Kaihuangchuan; the generals pursued the fugitives to Niujiazhai, where Alacu was wounded by an arrow and fled.

sentences.zh: 論功，進右都御史。

translations.literal: When merits were assessed, he was promoted to right censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When rewards were allotted for merit, he was promoted to right censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 又明年，越以方西征，辭大同巡撫。

translations.literal: The year after that, because he was then on a western campaign, Yue declined the post of grand coordinator of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Wang Yue, already engaged in the western campaign, asked to be relieved of the Datong grand coordinator post.

sentences.zh: 詔聽之，加總督軍務，專辦西事。

translations.literal: An edict granted this and added the title of supreme commander of military affairs, with sole charge of western affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed and added to his title supreme commander of military affairs, putting him in sole charge of the western front.

sentences.zh: 然是時寇數萬，而官軍堪戰者僅萬人，又分散防守，勢不敵。

translations.literal: Yet at this time the raiders numbered in the tens of thousands, while government troops fit for battle were only ten thousand, and they were moreover scattered in defense; the force was no match.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the raiders now numbered in the tens of thousands, while barely ten thousand government troops were fit for battle—and those were scattered across defensive posts. The odds were against them.

sentences.zh: 永、越乃條上戰、守二策。

translations.literal: Yong and Yue then submitted in detail the two plans of attack and defense.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yong and Wang Yue then submitted detailed proposals for both an offensive and a defensive strategy.

sentences.zh: 尚書白圭亦難之，請敕諸將守。

translations.literal: Minister Bai Gui also found it difficult and requested an edict ordering the generals to hold defense.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Bai Gui was likewise daunted by the prospect and asked that the generals be ordered to stand on the defensive.

sentences.zh: 其年，寇復連入懷遠諸堡，永、越禦卻之。

translations.literal: That year the raiders again entered in succession the forts around Huaiyuan; Yong and Yue repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: That year the raiders again broke into the forts around Huaiyuan in succession; Zhu Yong and Wang Yue drove them back.

sentences.zh: 圭復請大舉搜套。

translations.literal: Gui again requested a major sweep of the Ordos.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Gui again urged a major expedition to scour the Ordos region.

sentences.zh: 明年遣侍郎葉盛至軍議。

translations.literal: The next year Vice Minister Ye Sheng was sent to the army for consultation.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the court sent Vice Minister Ye Sheng to the front to consult with the command.

sentences.zh: 時永已召還，越以士卒衣裝盡壞，馬死過半，請且休兵，與盛偕還。

translations.literal: By then Yong had already been recalled; Yue, because the soldiers' clothing and gear were entirely ruined and more than half the horses had died, requested a temporary halt to operations and returned together with Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zhu Yong had already been recalled; Wang Yue reported that the men's clothing and equipment were in ruins and more than half the horses had died, asked for a temporary halt to operations, and returned to court with Ye Sheng.

sentences.zh: 而廷議以套不滅，三邊終無寧歲；

translations.literal: But court deliberation held that if the Ordos were not destroyed, the three border regions would never know a year of peace;
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion held, however, that unless the Ordos were cleared the three border regions would never see a year of peace;

sentences.zh: 先所調諸軍已逾八萬，將權不一，迄無成功。

translations.literal: the armies previously mobilized already exceeded eighty thousand, yet command was not unified and success had not been achieved.
translations.idiomatic: more than eighty thousand troops had already been mobilized, yet divided command had produced no success.

sentences.zh: 宜專遣大將調度。

translations.literal: It was fitting to dispatch a great general alone to direct operations.
translations.idiomatic: A single senior commander should be sent to take unified charge.

sentences.zh: 乃拜武靖侯趙輔為平虜將軍，敕陜西、寧夏、延綏三鎮兵皆受節制，越總督軍務。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Marquis of Wujing, Zhao Fu, was appointed Pacifier of the Barbarians General; an edict ordered that troops of the three garrisons of Shaanxi, Ningxia, and Yan-sui all accept his command, with Yue as supreme commander of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Wujing, Zhao Fu, was then appointed Pacifier of the Barbarians General; an edict placed the armies of the Shaanxi, Ningxia, and Yan-sui garrisons under his command, with Wang Yue as supreme commander of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 比至，寇方深入環慶、固原飽掠，軍竟無功。

translations.literal: By the time they arrived, the raiders had already penetrated deep into Huanqing and Guyuan and plundered their fill; the army in the end achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: By the time they arrived, the raiders had already driven deep into Huanqing and Guyuan and sacked them at leisure; the expedition accomplished nothing.

sentences.zh: 越、輔以滿都魯、孛羅忽、乚加思蘭方強盛，勢未可破，乃奏言：「欲窮搜河套，非調精兵十五萬不可。

translations.literal: Yue and Fu, because Mandul, Bolohu, and Ygasan were then flourishing in strength and the situation could not yet be broken, memorialized, saying, "To search out the Ordos to the end, one cannot do without mobilizing one hundred fifty thousand picked troops.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue and Zhao Fu reported that Mandul, Bolohu, and Ygasan were at the height of their power and could not yet be broken, and memorialized: "To scour the Ordos thoroughly would require no fewer than one hundred fifty thousand elite troops.

sentences.zh: 今饋餉煩勞，公私困竭，重加科斂，內釁可虞。

translations.literal: Now supply transport is burdensome, public and private resources are exhausted, and if levies are increased again, internal strife may be feared.
translations.idiomatic: Supply lines are already overstrained, public and private resources are exhausted, and further levies would risk unrest at home.

sentences.zh: 宜姑事退守，散遣士馬，量留精銳，就糧鄜、延，沿邊軍民悉令內徙。

translations.literal: It is fitting for the time being to withdraw to defense, disperse troops and horses, retain in measured numbers elite forces, draw grain from Fu and Yan, and order all border soldiers and civilians to move inward.
translations.idiomatic: For the present we should fall back to the defensive, disperse troops and horses, keep only a picked force supplied from Fu and Yan, and order all frontier soldiers and civilians to relocate inland.

sentences.zh: 其寇所出沒之所，多置烽燧，鑿塹築墻，以為保障。」

translations.literal: At the places where the raiders appear and vanish, beacons should be set up in great number, ditches dug and walls built, to serve as protection.
translations.idiomatic: Where the raiders come and go we should build more beacon towers, dig trenches, and raise walls as a defensive screen.

sentences.zh: 奏上，廷議不決。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, court deliberation reached no decision.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went up, but the court could not settle on a decision.

sentences.zh: 越等又奏：「寇知我軍大集，移營近河，潛謀北渡，殆不戰自屈。

translations.literal: Yue and the others memorialized again: "The raiders know our army is massed in strength; they have moved their camps near the river and secretly plan to cross north—likely they will yield without battle.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue and his colleagues memorialized again: "The raiders know our armies are massed; they have shifted camp toward the river and are secretly planning to cross north—they may well withdraw without a fight.

sentences.zh: 但山、陜荒旱，芻糧缺供，邊地早寒，凍餒相繼。

translations.literal: But the mountains and Shaanxi are stricken by drought; fodder and grain are lacking, the border lands grow cold early, and freezing and hunger follow one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: But the hills and fields of Shaanxi are stricken by drought, fodder and grain are running short, the frontier turns cold early, and men are succumbing to hunger and frost in succession.

sentences.zh: 以時度之，攻取實難，請從防守之策，臣等亦暫還朝。」

translations.literal: Judging by the season, attack is truly difficult; we ask to follow the plan of defense, and your ministers too will for the time return to court.
translations.idiomatic: Given the season, an offensive is impracticable; we ask permission to adopt the defensive plan and return temporarily to court.

sentences.zh: 於是部科諸臣劾越、輔欺謾。

translations.literal: Thereupon officials of the ministries and the censorate impeached Yue and Fu for deception.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon officials of the ministries and the censorate impeached Wang Yue and Zhao Fu for deceiving the throne.

sentences.zh: 會輔有疾，召還，以寧晉伯劉聚代。

translations.literal: As it happened Fu fell ill and was recalled; the Earl of Ningjin, Liu Ju, replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Fu then fell ill and was recalled; the Earl of Ningjin, Liu Ju, was appointed in his place.

sentences.zh: 明年，越與聚敗寇溫天嶺，進左都御史。

translations.literal: The next year Yue and Ju defeated the raiders at Wentian Ridge, and he was promoted to left censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Wang Yue and Liu Ju defeated the raiders at Wentian Ridge, and he was promoted to left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 是時三遣大將，皆以越總督軍務。

translations.literal: At this time three great generals were dispatched, and in each case Yue served as supreme commander of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: By then three senior generals had been sent to the front, and in every case Wang Yue served as supreme commander of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 寇每入，小擊輒去，軍罷即復來，率一歲數入。

translations.literal: Whenever the raiders entered, a small strike would send them away; once the army stood down they came again, as a rule several times in a year.
translations.idiomatic: Each time the raiders crossed the border a minor strike would drive them off, but once the army stood down they returned—several incursions in a year was the rule.

sentences.zh: 將士益玩寇，而寇勢轉熾。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers increasingly treated the raiders lightly, while the raiders' power turned ever fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: The troops grew ever more complacent toward the enemy, while the raiders grew bolder.

sentences.zh: 其年九月，滿都魯及孛羅忽、乚加思蘭留妻子老弱於紅鹽池，大舉深入，直抵秦州、安定諸州縣。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of that year Mandul, Bolohu, and Ygasan left wives, children, and the old and weak at Red Salt Pool and launched a major deep raid straight to the prefectures and counties of Qinzhou and Anding.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of that year Mandul, Bolohu, and Ygasan left their wives, children, and noncombatants at Red Salt Pool and launched a major raid deep into the interior, reaching as far as Qinzhou and Anding.

sentences.zh: 越策寇盡銳西，不備東偏，乃率延綏總兵官許寧、遊擊將軍周玉各將五千騎為左右哨，出榆林，逾紅兒山，涉白鹽灘，兩晝夜行八百里。

translations.literal: Yue calculated that the raiders had committed all their strength to the west and were unprepared on the eastern flank; he therefore led the Yan-sui commander-in-chief Xu Ning and the mobile commander Zhou Yu, each commanding five thousand horsemen as left and right vanguards, out from Yulin, over Hong'er Mountain, across White Salt Shoals, and in two days and nights marched eight hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue reasoned that the raiders had committed their full strength to the west and left their eastern flank exposed; he led the Yan-sui commander Xu Ning and the mobile commander Zhou Yu, each with five thousand horsemen as left and right vanguards, out from Yulin, over Hong'er Mountain and across White Salt Shoals, covering eight hundred li in two days and nights.

sentences.zh: 將至，暴風起，塵翳目。

translations.literal: Just before arrival a violent wind arose and dust blinded the eyes.
translations.idiomatic: As they were nearing their objective a violent wind sprang up and dust blotted out the sky.

sentences.zh: 一老卒前曰：「天贊我也。

translations.literal: An old soldier stepped forward and said, "Heaven is aiding us.
translations.idiomatic: An old soldier stepped forward and said, "Heaven is on our side.

sentences.zh: 去而風，使敵不覺。

translations.literal: Going with the wind, the enemy will not notice.
translations.idiomatic: March with the wind at our backs and the enemy will never know we are coming.

sentences.zh: 還軍，遇歸寇，處下風。

translations.literal: When the army returns and meets the raiders coming back, we will be to leeward.
translations.idiomatic: When we turn back and meet the raiders returning, we will have the wind at our backs.

sentences.zh: 乘風擊之，蔑不勝矣。」

translations.literal: Striking them riding the wind, none will fail to win.
translations.idiomatic: Strike with the wind behind us and we cannot fail to win.

sentences.zh: 越遽下馬拜之，擢為千戶。

translations.literal: Yue immediately dismounted and bowed to him, and promoted him to commander of a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue immediately dismounted and bowed to him, then promoted him on the spot to commander of a thousand.

sentences.zh: 分兵千為十覆，而身率寧、玉張兩翼，薄其營，大破之。

translations.literal: He divided one thousand men into ten ambushes, while he personally led Ning and Yu to spread the two wings, pressed close on their camp, and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: He split one thousand men into ten ambush parties, then personally led Xu Ning and Zhou Yu to deploy on both wings, closed on the enemy camp, and broke it completely.

sentences.zh: 擒斬三百五十，獲駝馬器械無算，焚其廬帳而還。

translations.literal: They captured and killed three hundred fifty, seized camels, horses, and weapons beyond counting, burned their tents and shelters, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: They killed or captured three hundred fifty men, took camels, horses, and weapons beyond count, burned the enemy encampment, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 及滿都魯等飽掠歸，則妻子畜產已蕩盡，相顧痛哭。

translations.literal: When Mandul and the others returned sated from plunder, their wives, children, and livestock had already been swept away; they looked at one another and wept bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: When Mandul and his men returned laden with plunder, they found their wives, children, and herds utterly destroyed; they looked at one another and wept.

sentences.zh: 自是遠徙北去，不敢復居河套，西陲息肩者數年。

translations.literal: From this they moved far north and did not dare again to dwell in the Ordos; the western frontier rested its shoulders for several years.
translations.idiomatic: From then on they moved far to the north and dared not settle in the Ordos again; the western frontier enjoyed several years of relief.

sentences.zh: 初，文臣視師者，率從大軍後，出號令行賞罰而已。

translations.literal: At first, when civil officials supervised armies, they generally followed behind the main force and issued orders and carried out rewards and punishments, and that was all.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, when civil officials supervised armies they usually followed in the rear of the main force, issuing orders and meting out rewards and punishments—and little else.

sentences.zh: 越始多選跳蕩士為腹心將，親與寇搏。

translations.literal: Yue was the first to choose many daring soldiers as trusted commanders and personally grapple with the raiders.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue was the first to pick out daring fighters as his trusted commanders and to engage the enemy in person.

sentences.zh: 又以間覘敵累重邀劫之，或剪其零騎，用是數有功。

translations.literal: He also used scouts to watch the enemy and repeatedly waylaid their baggage trains, or cut off their scattered horsemen; by this he won merit many times.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent scouts to track the enemy and repeatedly ambushed their supply trains, or picked off detached cavalry—by such means he won repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 十年春，廷議設總制府於固原，舉定西侯蔣琬為總兵官，越提督軍務，控制延綏、寧夏、甘肅三邊。

translations.literal: In the spring of the tenth year court deliberation proposed establishing a supreme command at Guyuan, recommending the Marquis of Dingxi, Jiang Wan, as commander-in-chief, with Yue supervising military affairs and controlling the three border regions of Yan-sui, Ningxia, and Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the tenth year the court proposed establishing a supreme command headquarters at Guyuan, nominating the Marquis of Dingxi, Jiang Wan, as commander-in-chief, with Wang Yue supervising military affairs over the three frontier regions of Yan-sui, Ningxia, and Gansu.

sentences.zh: 總兵、巡撫而下，並聽節制。

translations.literal: Commanders-in-chief, grand coordinators, and all below were to accept his regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders-in-chief, grand coordinators, and all officers below them were placed under his authority.

sentences.zh: 詔罷琬，即以越任之，三邊設總制自此始。

translations.literal: An edict dismissed Wan and directly appointed Yue in his place; the establishment of a supreme command over the three border regions began from this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict removed Jiang Wan and gave the post directly to Wang Yue—the post of supreme commander over the three frontier regions dates from this appointment.

sentences.zh: 論功，加太子少保，增俸一級。

translations.literal: When merits were assessed, he was given the additional title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and one step increase in salary.
translations.idiomatic: When rewards were allotted for merit, he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given one step in salary.

sentences.zh: 紀功郎中張謹、兵科給事中郭鏜等論劉聚等濫殺冒功，並劾越妄奏。

translations.literal: Zhang Jin, a director in the merit-recording office, Guo Tang, a supervising secretary in the military section of the censorate, and others argued that Liu Ju and others had killed wantonly and falsely claimed merit, and also impeached Yue for reckless memorializing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jin of the merit-recording office and Guo Tang, a supervising secretary in the military section of the censorate, charged Liu Ju and others with indiscriminate killing and false claims of merit, and also impeached Wang Yue for reckless memorializing.

sentences.zh: 越方自以功大賞薄，遂怏怏，稱疾還朝。

translations.literal: Yue just then considered his merit great and his reward slight; he became resentful, pleaded illness, and returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue, feeling his achievements had outstripped his rewards, grew resentful, pleaded illness, and returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 明年與左都御史李賓同掌院事，兼督十二團營。

translations.literal: The next year he joined Left Censor-in-Chief Li Bin in directing the Censorate and concurrently supervised the Twelve Regiments.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he joined Left Censor-in-Chief Li Bin in directing the Censorate and was also put in charge of the Twelve Regiments.

sentences.zh: 越素以才自喜，不修小節，為朝議所齮。

translations.literal: Yue had always prided himself on his talent and did not cultivate small proprieties; he was gnawed at by court opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue had always been proud of his ability and disdained petty proprieties, and court opinion had long been set against him.

sentences.zh: 至是乃破名檢，與群小關通。

translations.literal: At this point he broke moral restraint and connected with petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Now he cast off all restraint and consorted with unsavory characters.

sentences.zh: 奸人韋英者，以官奴從征延綏，冒功得百戶。

translations.literal: A villain named Wei Ying, as a government slave accompanying the campaign in Yan-sui, falsely claimed merit and received the rank of commander of a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: One such man was the schemer Wei Ying, who had gone to Yan-sui as a government bondsman, falsely claimed military merit, and been granted the rank of commander of a hundred households.

sentences.zh: 汪直掌西廠用事，英為爪牙，趙因英自結於直。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi controlled the Western Depot and wielded power; Ying served as his claws and teeth; through Ying he attached himself to Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi ran the Western Depot and wielded real power; Wei Ying served as his henchman, and Wang Yue used Ying to cultivate ties with Zhi.

sentences.zh: 內閣論罷西廠，越遇大學士劉吉、劉珝於朝，顯謂之曰：「汪直行事亦甚公。

translations.literal: When the Grand Secretariat deliberated on abolishing the Western Depot, Yue met Grand Secretaries Liu Ji and Liu Bing at court and said openly to them, "Wang Zhi in his conduct is also quite fair.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Secretariat debated abolishing the Western Depot, Wang Yue encountered Grand Secretaries Liu Ji and Liu Bing at court and said openly, "Wang Zhi's conduct is quite fair.

sentences.zh: 如黃賜專權納賂，非直不能去。

translations.literal: For example, Huang Ci monopolized power and accepted bribes; without Zhi he could not have been removed.
translations.idiomatic: Take Huang Ci, who monopolized power and took bribes—without Wang Zhi he could never have been removed.

sentences.zh: 商、萬在事久，是非多有所忌憚。

translations.literal: Shang and Wan have long been in office; on right and wrong they have many things they fear and dread.
translations.idiomatic: Shang and Wan have been in power for years; on matters of right and wrong they have too much to lose.

sentences.zh: 二公入閣幾日，何亦為此？」

translations.literal: You two gentlemen have entered the Secretariat only a few days—why also do this?
translations.idiomatic: You two have only just entered the Grand Secretariat—why take this line yourselves?

sentences.zh: 珝曰：「吾輩所言，非為身謀。

translations.literal: Bing said, "What we speak of is not scheming for ourselves.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bing replied, "What we say is not for our own advantage.

sentences.zh: 使值行事皆公，朝廷置公卿大夫何為？」

translations.literal: If eunuchs in their conduct were all fair, for what would the court appoint grand ministers and great officers?"
translations.idiomatic: If eunuchs could be trusted to act fairly in every case, what need would the court have for its grand ministers and high officials?"

sentences.zh: 越不能對。

translations.literal: Yue could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue had no answer.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書項忠罷，越當遷，而朝命予陜西巡撫余子俊。

translations.literal: Minister of War Xiang Zhong was dismissed; Yue ought to have been promoted, but the court appointed Yu Zijun as Grand Coordinator of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister of War Xiang Zhong was removed from office, Wang Yue should have been promoted, but the court instead named Yu Zijun Grand Coordinator of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 越彌不平，請解營務，優詔不許。

translations.literal: Yue was all the more resentful and asked to be relieved of camp duties; a gracious edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue grew still more indignant and asked to be relieved of his camp command, but an edict of special favor refused the request.

sentences.zh: 因自陳搗巢功，為故尚書白圭所抑，從征將士多未錄，乞移所加官酬之。

translations.literal: He then memorialized on his own behalf regarding the merit of raiding enemy nests, saying it had been suppressed by the late Minister Bai Gui, that many officers and soldiers who joined the campaign had not been recorded, and begging to transfer the offices conferred on him to reward them.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial on his own behalf, stating that credit for the nest-raiding campaign had been withheld by the late Minister Bai Gui and that many officers and soldiers who had fought under him had gone unrewarded; he asked that the offices recently granted him be transferred to compensate them.

sentences.zh: 子俊亦言越賞不酬功，乃進兵部尚書，仍掌院事。

translations.literal: Zijun also said Yue's rewards did not match his merits; thereupon he was promoted to Minister of War while still administering the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zijun likewise reported that Wang Yue's rewards did not match his achievements, and so Yue was promoted to Minister of War while continuing to head the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 尋加太子太保。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was given the additional title of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given the additional title of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 越急功名。

translations.literal: Yue was impatient for fame and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue was driven by an urgent hunger for fame and glory.

sentences.zh: 汪直初東征，越望督師，為陳鉞所沮。

translations.literal: When Wang Zhi first campaigned east, Yue hoped to command the army but was thwarted by Chen Yue.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Zhi first led an eastern campaign, Wang Yue hoped to take overall command, but Chen Yue blocked him.

sentences.zh: 鉞驟寵，心益艷之。

translations.literal: Chen Yue suddenly gained favor; Wang Yue's heart grew all the more envious of this.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yue suddenly rose in favor, and Wang Yue's envy only grew keener.

sentences.zh: 十六年春，延綏守臣奏寇潛渡河入靖虜，越乃說直出師。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixteenth year, the defending officials of Yan-sui reported that raiders had secretly crossed the river into Jing-lu; Yue then persuaded Zhi to take the field.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixteenth year, the frontier officials of Yan-sui reported that raiders had secretly crossed the river into Jing-lu, and Wang Yue persuaded Wang Zhi to take the field.

sentences.zh: 詔拜保國公朱永為平虜將軍，直監軍，而越提督軍務。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Duke of Protecting the State Zhu Yong General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, with Zhi supervising the army and Yue directing military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed the Duke of Protecting the State, Zhu Yong, General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, with Wang Zhi supervising the army and Wang Yue directing military affairs.

sentences.zh: 越說直令永率大軍由南路，己與直將輕騎循塞垣而西，俱會榆林。
