translations.literal: Yue persuaded Zhi to have Yong lead the main army by the southern route while he and Zhi led light cavalry along the border ramparts westward, all to meet at Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue persuaded Wang Zhi to have Zhu Yong lead the main force by the southern route while he and Zhi themselves led light cavalry west along the border wall, all to rendezvous at Yulin.

sentences.zh: 越至大同，聞敵帳在威寧海子，則盡選宣、大兩鎮兵二萬，出孤店，潛行至貓兒莊，分數道。

translations.literal: When Yue reached Datong and heard the enemy camp was at Weining Lake, he selected all twenty thousand troops from the Xuan and Da garrisons, went out from Gudian, stealthily marched to Mao'erzhuang, and divided into several routes.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Yue reached Datong and learned that the enemy camp lay at Weining Lake, he mustered all twenty thousand troops from the Xuanfu and Datong garrisons, marched out from Gudian, stole up to Mao'erzhuang by secret routes, and divided his force into several columns.

sentences.zh: 值大風雨雪晦冥，進至威寧，寇猶不覺，掩擊大破之。

translations.literal: They encountered great wind and snow with sky dark and dim; advancing to Weining, the raiders still did not notice; a surprise attack utterly routed them.
translations.idiomatic: A fierce snowstorm blotted out the sky; they pressed on to Weining while the raiders still had no inkling of their approach, then fell upon them in a surprise attack and broke them completely.

sentences.zh: 斬首四百三十余級，獲馬駝牛羊六千，師不至榆林而還。

translations.literal: They cut off more than four hundred thirty heads, seized six thousand horses, camels, cattle, and sheep, and the army returned without reaching Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: They took more than four hundred thirty heads, captured six thousand horses, camels, cattle, and sheep, and withdrew without ever reaching Yulin.

sentences.zh: 永所出道迂，不見敵，無功。

translations.literal: The route by which Yong went was circuitous; he did not see the enemy and achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yong's column took a roundabout route, never encountered the enemy, and won no success.

sentences.zh: 由是封越威寧伯，世襲，歲祿千二百石。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yue was enfeoffed as Marquis of Weining, hereditary, with an annual stipend of twelve hundred shi.
translations.idiomatic: For this Wang Yue was enfeoffed as Marquis of Weining with a hereditary title and an annual stipend of twelve hundred shi.

sentences.zh: 越受封，不當復領都察院，而越不欲就西班。

translations.literal: Having received enfeoffment, Yue ought not again to head the Censorate, yet Yue did not wish to take his place among the western rank.
translations.idiomatic: Once ennobled, Wang Yue should no longer have headed the Censorate, but he was unwilling to take his place among the civil officials of the western rank.

sentences.zh: 御史許進等頌其功，引王驥、楊善例，請仍領院事，提督團營。

translations.literal: Censor Xu Jin and others praised his merits, citing the precedents of Wang Ji and Yang Shan, and asked that he still head the Censorate and direct the regiment camps.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Xu Jin and others praised his achievements, citing the precedents of Wang Ji and Yang Shan, and asked that he continue to head the Censorate and direct the regiment camps.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 明年復與直、永帥師出大同。

translations.literal: The next year he again led troops out from Datong with Zhi and Yong.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he again led an army out from Datong with Wang Zhi and Zhu Yong.

sentences.zh: 適寇入掠，追擊至黑石崖，擒斬百二十余人，獲馬七百匹。

translations.literal: Just then raiders entered to plunder; pursuing them to Black Stone Cliff, they captured and killed more than one hundred twenty men and seized seven hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: Raiders happened to cross the border on a plundering raid; pursuing them to Black Stone Cliff, the army killed or captured more than one hundred twenty men and took seven hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 進太子太傅，增歲祿四百石。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, with four hundred shi added to his annual stipend.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and four hundred shi were added to his annual stipend.

sentences.zh: 明制，文臣不得封公侯。

translations.literal: Under Ming institutions, civil officials could not be enfeoffed as duke or marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Under Ming law, civil officials could not be enfeoffed as duke or marquis.

sentences.zh: 越從勛臣例，改掌前軍都督府，總五軍營兵，督團營如故。

translations.literal: Yue followed the precedent for meritorious nobles, transferred to head the Front Army Command Headquarters, commanded the troops of the Five Armies Camps, and directed the regiment camps as before.
translations.idiomatic: Following the precedent set for meritorious nobles, Wang Yue was transferred to head the Front Army Command Headquarters, given overall command of the Five Armies Camps, and continued to direct the regiment camps as before.

sentences.zh: 自是真為武人，且望侯矣。

translations.literal: From this he truly became a military man, and moreover looked toward a marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: From that point he was truly a military man, and he already had his eye on a marquisate.

sentences.zh: 其年五月，宣府告警，命佩平胡將軍印，充總兵官。

translations.literal: That year in the fifth month, when Xuanfu raised an alarm, he was ordered to wear the seal of General Who Pacifies the Hu, serving as overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, when Xuanfu sounded the alarm in the fifth month, he was ordered to wear the seal of General Who Pacifies the Hu and serve as overall commander.

sentences.zh: 復以直監督軍務，率京軍萬人赴之。

translations.literal: Again Zhi was to supervise military affairs; he led ten thousand capital troops to go there.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi was again placed in charge of supervising military affairs, and Wang Yue led ten thousand capital troops to the scene.

sentences.zh: 比至，寇已去，因留屯其地。

translations.literal: By the time they arrived the raiders had already gone, so they remained and garrisoned the place.
translations.idiomatic: By the time they arrived the raiders had already withdrawn, so they remained and garrisoned the area.

sentences.zh: 至冬，而直為其儕所間，寵衰。

translations.literal: By winter, Zhi had been slandered by his peers and his favor waned.
translations.idiomatic: By winter Wang Zhi had been undermined by his rivals at court, and imperial favor toward him waned.

sentences.zh: 越等再請班師，不許。

translations.literal: Yue and the others again asked to withdraw the army; permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue and the others again asked to withdraw the army, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 陳鉞居兵部，亦代直請。

translations.literal: Chen Yue held the Ministry of War and also asked on Zhi's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yue, who now headed the Ministry of War, also petitioned on Wang Zhi's behalf.

sentences.zh: 帝切責之，兩人始懼。

translations.literal: The emperor sharply rebuked them; only then did the two men grow afraid.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sharply rebuked them, and only then did the two men begin to fear for themselves.

sentences.zh: 已，大同總兵官孫鉞卒，即命越代之，而以直總鎮大同、宣府，悉召京營將士還。

translations.literal: Presently the overall commander of Datong, Sun Yue, died; Yue was immediately ordered to replace him, while Zhi was put in overall charge of Datong and Xuanfu, and all capital-camp officers and soldiers were summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the overall commander of Datong, Sun Yue, died; Wang Yue was immediately ordered to replace him, while Wang Zhi was given overall charge of Datong and Xuanfu and all capital-camp officers and soldiers were recalled.

sentences.zh: 明年，寇犯延綏。

translations.literal: The next year raiders violated Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: The following year raiders struck Yan-sui.

sentences.zh: 越等調兵援之，頗有斬獲，益祿五十石。

translations.literal: Yue and the others transferred troops to relieve them and achieved considerable kills and captures; fifty shi were added to his stipend.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue and his subordinates shifted troops to the relief and won a fair number of kills and captures; fifty shi were added to his stipend.

sentences.zh: 帝是時益知越、直交結狀。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor came to know all the more the state of Yue's and Zhi's mutual collusion.
translations.idiomatic: By this time the emperor understood more clearly how closely Wang Yue and Wang Zhi were allied.

sentences.zh: 大學士萬安等以越有智計，恐誘直復進，乃請調越延綏以離之。

translations.literal: Grand Secretaries Wan An and others, because Yue had schemes and stratagems, feared he would induce Zhi to rise again and therefore asked that Yue be transferred to Yan-sui to separate them.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretaries Wan An and others, knowing Wang Yue's cunning, feared he would draw Wang Zhi back into power and therefore asked that Yue be transferred to Yan-sui to break the alliance.

sentences.zh: 兩人勢益衰。

translations.literal: The power of the two men grew all the more feeble.
translations.idiomatic: The influence of the two men declined still further.

sentences.zh: 明年，直得罪，言官並劾越。

translations.literal: The next year Zhi fell from grace; censorial officials jointly impeached Yue.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Wang Zhi fell from grace, and censorial officials impeached Wang Yue along with him.

sentences.zh: 詔奪爵除名，謫居安陸，三子以功蔭得官者，皆削籍，且使使賫敕諭之。

translations.literal: An edict stripped his title and removed his name from the rolls, banished him to live in Anlu, the three sons who had received offices through inherited merit were all removed from the registers, and moreover envoys were sent bearing an edict to instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stripped him of his title and removed his name from the rolls, banished him to Anlu, struck from the registers all three sons who had received office through inherited merit, and sent envoys bearing an imperial instruction to read the decree to him.

sentences.zh: 越聞使至，欲自裁，見敕有從輕語，乃稍自安。

translations.literal: When Yue heard the envoys had arrived he wished to take his own life; seeing the edict contained lenient wording, he then grew somewhat reassured.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Yue heard the envoys had arrived he was ready to take his own life, but when he saw that the edict contained language of leniency he grew somewhat reassured.

sentences.zh: 越既為禮法士所疾，自負豪傑，驁然自如。

translations.literal: Yue had long been detested by men of ritual and law; confident in himself as a heroic figure, he remained arrogantly at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue had long been resented by men of propriety and learning; confident in his own heroic stature, he carried himself with arrogant ease.

sentences.zh: 飲食供奉擬王者，射獵聲樂自恣，雖謫徙不少衰。

translations.literal: His food and drink and retinue rivaled a king's; he indulged freely in hunting, music, and pleasure—even in banishment and removal his scale did not diminish much.
translations.idiomatic: His table and retinue rivaled a king's; he indulged freely in hunting, music, and pleasure, and even in exile his style of living scarcely diminished.

sentences.zh: 故其得罪，時議頗謂太過，而竟無白之者。

translations.literal: Therefore when he fell from grace, contemporary opinion largely considered it excessive, yet in the end there was no one to speak on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason many at the time felt his punishment had gone too far, yet in the end no one spoke up for him.

sentences.zh: 孝宗立，赦還。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong acceded, he was pardoned and allowed to return.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xiaozong Emperor came to the throne, he was pardoned and allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 弘治七年，越屢疏訟冤。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Hongzhi, Yue repeatedly memorialized to plead his innocence.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Hongzhi reign, Wang Yue repeatedly submitted memorials pleading his innocence.

sentences.zh: 詔復左都御史，致仕。

translations.literal: An edict restored him to Left Censor-in-Chief and granted retirement.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored him to the post of Left Censor-in-Chief and granted him retirement.

sentences.zh: 越年七十，耄矣，復結中官李廣，以中旨召掌都察院事。

translations.literal: Yue was seventy years old—senile indeed—yet again attached himself to the eunuch Li Guang and, by secret imperial rescript, was summoned to administer the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue was seventy years old and already in his dotage, yet he again attached himself to the eunuch Li Guang and, by secret rescript, was summoned back to head the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 給事中季源、御史王一言等交章論，乃寢。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Ji Yuan, Censor Wang Yiyan, and others submitted successive memorials in opposition, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Ji Yuan, Censor Wang Yiyan, and others submitted successive memorials in protest, and the appointment was dropped.

sentences.zh: 十年冬寇犯甘肅。

translations.literal: In the winter of the tenth year raiders violated Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the tenth year raiders struck Gansu.

sentences.zh: 廷議復設總制官，先後會舉七人，不稱旨。

translations.literal: At court they debated reestablishing the post of overall controller; in succession seven men were jointly recommended, but none pleased the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: At court they debated reestablishing the post of overall frontier controller; seven candidates were recommended in turn, but none satisfied the emperor.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書屠滽以越名上，乃詔起原官，加太子太保，總制甘、涼邊務兼巡撫。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Tu Yong submitted Yue's name; an edict then recalled him to his former office, added Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and put him in overall charge of Gansu and Liangzhou border affairs while also serving as Grand Coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Tu Yong submitted Wang Yue's name; an edict then recalled him to his former rank, added the title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and put him in overall charge of the Gansu and Liangzhou frontier while also serving as Grand Coordinator.

sentences.zh: 越言甘鎮兵弱，非籍延、寧兩鎮兵難以克敵，請兼制兩鎮，解巡撫事。

translations.literal: Yue said the Gansu garrison was weak and that without drawing on the troops of the Yan and Ning garrisons it would be hard to defeat the enemy; he asked to command both garrisons as well and to be relieved of Grand Coordinator duties.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue argued that the Gansu garrison was too weak and that the enemy could not be defeated without troops from the Yan-sui and Ningxia garrisons; he asked to command both garrisons as well and to be relieved of his duties as Grand Coordinator.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 明年，越以寇巢賀蘭山後，數擾邊，乃分兵三路進剿。

translations.literal: The next year, because the raiders were encamped behind Helan Mountain and repeatedly harassed the border, Yue divided his forces into three routes and advanced to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, with the raiders encamped behind Helan Mountain and repeatedly harassing the frontier, Wang Yue divided his force into three columns and advanced to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 斬四十三級，獲馬駝百余。

translations.literal: They cut off forty-three heads and seized more than one hundred horses and camels.
translations.idiomatic: They took forty-three heads and captured more than one hundred horses and camels.

sentences.zh: 加少保，兼太子太傅。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title of Junior Guardian and concurrently made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Junior Guardian and concurrently made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 遂條上制置哈密事宜。

translations.literal: He then submitted in detail arrangements for administering Hami.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a detailed plan for administering Hami.

sentences.zh: 會李廣得罪死，言官連章劾廣黨，皆及越。

translations.literal: Just then Li Guang fell from grace and died; censorial officials submitted successive memorials impeaching Li Guang's faction, all of which implicated Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Li Guang fell from grace and died; censorial officials submitted a stream of memorials impeaching Li Guang's faction, and all of them implicated Wang Yue.

sentences.zh: 越聞憂恨，其冬卒於甘州。

translations.literal: When Yue heard this he was grieved and resentful; that winter he died at Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Yue heard the news he was stricken with grief and resentment, and that winter he died at Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅，謚襄敏。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title of Grand Mentor and the posthumous name Xiangmin.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Grand Mentor and given the posthumous name Xiangmin.

sentences.zh: 越姿表奇偉，議論飆舉。

translations.literal: Yue's bearing was singularly imposing and his discourse swift and soaring.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue had a singularly imposing presence, and his speech was swift and forceful.

sentences.zh: 久歷邊陲，身經十余戰，知敵情偽及將士勇怯，出奇制勝，動有成算。

translations.literal: Long experienced on the frontier, he personally went through more than ten battles, knew the enemy's falsehoods and truth and the courage or cowardice of officers and soldiers; deploying surprises to overcome the foe, his moves generally had a settled plan.
translations.idiomatic: Long seasoned on the frontier, he had personally fought more than ten battles; he knew the enemy's deceptions and the courage or cowardice of his officers and men, and by striking with surprise he almost always won with a plan already in hand.

sentences.zh: 獎拔士類，籠罩豪俊，用財若流水，以故人樂為用。

translations.literal: He rewarded and promoted scholars, drew bold talents under his wing, spent wealth like flowing water—therefore men gladly served him.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded and promoted men of talent, gathered bold spirits under his command, and spent money like water, so that men were glad to serve him.

sentences.zh: 又嘗薦楊守隨、鐘、屠滽輩，皆有名於世。

translations.literal: He had also recommended Yang Shousui, Zhong, Tu Yong, and others, all renowned in their day.
translations.idiomatic: He had also recommended Yang Shousui, Zhong Qi, Tu Yong, and others, all of whom won renown in their time.

sentences.zh: 睦族敦舊，振窮恤貧，如恐不及。

translations.literal: He was kind to his clan and warm to old friends, relieved the destitute and succored the poor, as if fearing he would not reach them in time.
translations.idiomatic: He was devoted to his clan and loyal to old friends, relieving the destitute and succoring the poor as if he feared he might not reach them in time.

sentences.zh: 其膽智過絕於人。

translations.literal: His courage and wisdom surpassed others utterly.
translations.idiomatic: His courage and wit were beyond ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 嘗與朱永帥千人巡邊，寇猝至，永欲走，越止之，列陣自固，寇疑未敢前。

translations.literal: Once he and Zhu Yong led a thousand men on a border patrol when raiders suddenly arrived; Yong wished to flee, but Yue stopped him, formed ranks and fortified themselves—the raiders suspected a trap and did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while leading a thousand men on a border patrol with Zhu Yong, he was suddenly set upon by raiders; Yong wanted to flee, but Wang Yue stopped him, formed ranks, and held firm—the raiders suspected a trap and did not dare advance.

sentences.zh: 薄暮，令騎皆下馬，銜枚魚貫行，自率驍勇為殿，從山後行五十里抵城，謂永曰：「我一動，寇追擊，無噍類矣，示暇以惑之也。

translations.literal: At dusk he ordered all riders to dismount, march silently in single file with bits in their mouths; he personally led the crack troops as rearguard, went fifty li behind the mountains to reach the city, and said to Yong, "If I made one move the raiders would pursue and none would survive; I showed leisure to confuse them.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk he ordered every rider to dismount and march in single file with bits in their mouths; he personally led the crack troops as rearguard and, going fifty li behind the mountains, reached the city. He said to Yong, "If I had made one move the raiders would have pursued and none of us would have survived; I showed ease to confuse them.

sentences.zh: 下馬行，無軍聲，令寇不覺耳。」

translations.literal: Marching on foot there is no sound of an army—that is how to keep the enemy from noticing."
translations.idiomatic: March on foot and there is no sound of an army—that is how you keep the enemy from noticing."

sentences.zh: 性故豪縱。

translations.literal: By nature he was willful and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was bold and unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 嘗西行謁秦王，王開筵奏妓。

translations.literal: Once traveling west he called on the Prince of Qin; the prince spread a banquet with musicians performing.
translations.idiomatic: Once, traveling west, he paid a call on the Prince of Qin, who spread a banquet with musicians performing.

sentences.zh: 越語王：「下官為王吠犬久矣，寧無以相酬者？」

translations.literal: Yue said to the prince, "Your humble servant has long been the prince's hunting hound—is there nothing with which to reward me?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue said to the prince, "Your humble servant has long served as the prince's hunting hound—is there nothing with which to reward me?"

sentences.zh: 因盡乞其妓女以歸。

translations.literal: Thereupon he begged for all the courtesans and took them home.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he asked for all the courtesans and took them home with him.

sentences.zh: 一夕大雪，方圍爐飲，諸妓擁琵琶侍。

translations.literal: One evening during heavy snow, as he was drinking around the brazier, the courtesans attended him holding pipas.
translations.idiomatic: One snowy evening, as he was drinking around the brazier, the courtesans attended him with pipas in their arms.

sentences.zh: 一小校诇敵還，陳敵情。

translations.literal: A junior officer returned from scouting the enemy and reported on the enemy situation.
translations.idiomatic: A junior officer returned from scouting the enemy and reported what he had found.

sentences.zh: 未竟，越大喜，酌金卮飲之，命彈琵琶侑酒，即以金卮賜之。

translations.literal: Before he had finished, Yue was greatly pleased; he poured from a golden goblet for him to drink, ordered a pipa played to accompany the wine, and immediately bestowed the golden goblet on him.
translations.idiomatic: Before the report was finished Wang Yue was delighted; he poured wine from a golden goblet for the man to drink, ordered a pipa played to accompany the wine, and immediately gave him the goblet.

sentences.zh: 語畢益喜，指妓絕麗者目之曰：「若得此何如？」

translations.literal: When the report was finished he was still more delighted; pointing at an exceptionally beautiful courtesan he looked at the officer and said, "If you could have her, how would that be?"
translations.idiomatic: When the report was finished he was still more pleased; pointing at an exceptionally beautiful courtesan he looked at the officer and said, "If you could have her, how would that suit you?"

sentences.zh: 校惶恐謝。

translations.literal: The officer fearfully declined.
translations.idiomatic: The officer fearfully declined.

sentences.zh: 越大笑，立予之。

translations.literal: Yue laughed loudly and immediately gave her to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue laughed heartily and immediately gave her to him.

sentences.zh: 校所至為盡死力。

translations.literal: Wherever that officer went he exhausted himself in service.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever that officer went afterward, he gave his utmost in service.

sentences.zh: 越在時，人多咎其貪功。

translations.literal: While Yue was alive many blamed him for grasping after merit.
translations.idiomatic: While Wang Yue was alive many blamed him for grasping after credit.

sentences.zh: 及死，而將餒卒惰，冒功糜餉滋甚，邊臣竟未有如越者。

translations.literal: After his death, generals grew lax and soldiers idle; false claims of merit and waste of provisions grew ever worse—among frontier officials there was ultimately none like Yue.
translations.idiomatic: After his death, generals grew slack and soldiers lazy; false claims of merit and waste of rations grew worse than ever, and among frontier officials there was ultimately no one to match him.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：人非有才之難，而善用其才之難。

translations.literal: Commentary: It is not that talent is hard to come by, but that using talent well is hard.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The difficulty is not in finding talent, but in using it well.

sentences.zh: 王驥、王越之將兵，楊善之奉使，徐有貞之治河，其才皆有過人者。

translations.literal: Wang Ji's command of troops, Wang Yue's generalship, Yang Shan's diplomatic missions, and Xu Youzhen's river engineering—all had talent surpassing others.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji's command of troops, Wang Yue's generalship, Yang Shan's diplomatic missions, and Xu Youzhen's river works—all possessed talent beyond the ordinary.

sentences.zh: 假使隨流平進，以幹略自奮，不失為名卿大夫。

translations.literal: Had they followed the current and advanced smoothly, striving by their own capacity and strategy, they would not have fallen short of being renowned ministers and great officers.
translations.idiomatic: Had they gone with the flow and risen steadily, relying on their own ability and resolve, they would not have fallen short of becoming renowned ministers and great officers.

sentences.zh: 而顧以躁於進取，依附攀援，雖剖符受封，在文臣為希世之遇，而譽望因之隳損，甚亦不免削奪。

translations.literal: Yet they were instead restless in advancement, attaching themselves and climbing by patronage; although they received seals and enfeoffment—a rare fortune for civil officials—their reputation and standing were thereby ruined, and in the end they could not escape stripping and confiscation.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they were instead impatient for advancement, attaching themselves to powerful patrons and climbing by connection; though they received seals and enfeoffment—a rare honor for a civil official—their reputations were ruined in the process, and in the end many lost even what they had gained.

sentences.zh: 名節所系，可不重哉！

translations.literal: Repute and integrity are what hang in the balance—can they not be held weighty!
translations.idiomatic: Reputation and integrity hang in the balance—can they not be held sacred!
